summary: The construction and all three no-go conclusions are mathematically sound. The simplex cap bound, the accepted aggregate depth inequality, and its equality case make each actual top section exactly the singleton centroid; linear independence of the centroid vectors then gives proper ambient halfspaces realizing every top-point pattern. Downward closure on each lifted integer fiber proves the exact miss-intersection rule. The fractional-Helly example has the stated second-moment lower bound, the labelled-copy conditioning loses at most 1/8, and the exact intersection rule gives the sharp common-subfamily fraction r/N. Finally, for any fixed lift dimension and halfspace complexity, the arrangement-face bound makes the number of Boolean-combination patterns polynomial in N, contradicting the 2^N miss patterns for large R.
